abstract: Phosphate deficiency and salinity can coincide, but how roots integrate the two stresses is poorly understood. Root hairs (RHs) elongate under low inorganic phosphate and are inhibited by salt. Screening {beta}-estradiol-inducible TRANSPLANTA lines for 18 RH-expressed transcription factors (TFs) in Arabidopsis (Arabidopsis thaliana), we found that induction of ROOT HAIR DEFECTIVE 6 (RHD6) maintained RH growth under combined low phosphate (5 {micro}M) and salt (100 mM NaCl), which inhibited wild-type RH growth. RNA sequencing of RHD6-induced roots under dual stress identified 1,811 differentially expressed genes. Up-regulated genes were enriched for RH differentiation, tip growth and cell wall organization; down-regulated genes were enriched for phenylpropanoid and suberin metabolism, hydrogen peroxide catabolism, photosynthesis and responses to wounding and jasmonic acid. Promoter motif scanning combined with ensemble co-expression analysis defined a core network of 396 candidate direct RHD6 targets, including 31 TFs. The TFs with the largest expression changes were HEC3, HEC1 and EIL4. In T-DNA insertion mutants, dual stress did not shorten hec3 RHs; eil4 and hec1 had shorter RHs on the control medium but no significant change in relative inhibition. These data provide a resource of RHD6-dependent genes and identify HEC3 as a modulator of the RH response to combined stress.
